questions.q: Which term describes the process by which an immigrant group adopts the dietary habits of the host country, often leading to increased intake of processed foods and fats in the US?
questions.explain: Acculturation (or dietary acculturation) refers to adopting the eating patterns of the host country. In the US, this often correlates with negative health outcomes due to the 'Western diet'.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A patient following a **Kosher** (Jewish) diet would strictly avoid which of the following combinations?
questions.explain: Kosher laws (Kashrut) prohibit the consumption of meat and dairy products in the same meal. A cheeseburger mixes beef and cheese, which is forbidden.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: During the month of **Ramadan**, Muslims observe fasting (sawm) by abstaining from food and drink:
options: All day and night for 30 days
questions.explain: Ramadan fasting involves total abstinence from food and fluids from dawn (fajr) until sunset (maghrib).
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of the traditional **Mediterranean Diet**?
options: Butter as the primary added fat
High intake of olive oil, fruits, and vegetables
questions.explain: The Mediterranean Diet is characterized by plant-based foods, healthy fats (olive oil), moderate fish/poultry, and very limited red meat and sweets.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A **Food Desert** is best defined as:
options: An area with an overabundance of restaurants
A region where agriculture is impossible due to climate
A geographic area with limited access to affordable, nutritious food
A diet lacking in dessert foods
questions.explain: Food deserts are urban or rural areas where residents lack access to affordable, healthy food options (like grocery stores), often relying on convenience stores with processed foods.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Which nutrient is most likely to be deficient in a strict **Vegan** diet if not supplemented?
questions.explain: Vitamin B12 is found naturally only in animal products. Vegans must consume fortified foods or supplements to avoid anemia and neurological damage.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: In traditional **Asian** dietary patterns, which food group is typically consumed in much lower quantities compared to the Western diet, often due to high rates of intolerance?
questions.explain: Many Asian populations have a high prevalence of lactose intolerance, so dairy is not a traditional staple (calcium is often sourced from tofu, greens, or fish bones).
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: For a patient following a **Halal** diet, which of the following items is strictly prohibited?
questions.explain: Halal guidelines (Islamic dietary laws) strictly prohibit pork (swine) and intoxicants like alcohol. Most seafood is permitted (unlike strict Kosher rules which ban shellfish).
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: Members of the **Seventh-day Adventist** church typically follow which dietary pattern?
questions.explain: Seventh-day Adventists are encouraged to follow a vegetarian diet (often lacto-ovo). They also typically avoid alcohol, caffeine, and tobacco.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: The concept of 'Hot' and 'Cold' foods (unrelated to temperature) to balance the body's humors is a traditional belief common in which culture?
questions.explain: The hot-cold theory of health (derived from humoral medicine) is prevalent in many Hispanic/Latino and Asian cultures, where illnesses are treated with foods of the opposing quality.
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: A traditional **Hindu** diet usually avoids beef primarily because:
questions.explain: In Hinduism, the cow is revered as a symbol of life and is considered sacred, leading to the strict avoidance of beef (and often vegetarianism to practice Ahimsa/non-violence).
questions.exam: HOSA Nutrition: Dietary Epidemiology & Food Safety
questions.subject: Nutrition

questions.q: When counseling a client from a different culture, what is the first step in providing culturally competent care?
options: Hand them a standard meal plan
Assess their personal food habits and preferences
Tell them their traditional foods are unhealthy
Assume they eat only traditional foods
questions.explain: Cultural competence begins with assessment—asking questions to understand the individual's specific acculturation level, preferences, and constraints, rather than making assumptions.
